rv.q: Right from the wordless opening sequence of Hytner's superlative modern-day production, a reception at an art gallery for the opening of the 'Timon Room', we realise with delight that we're in for a treat.

Hytner's updated production gives each character sharp definition and turns one of Shakespeare's least treasured works into a powerful comment on the insulating effect of wealth and the precariousness of a credit culture in which reality is kept at bay.
Simon Russell Beale is a masterful Timon, all back-slapping bonhomie at the start but fearsome in the depths of his misanthropic misery.
What looks to be a surprise domestic hit will be exported via worldwide live broadcast screenings on Nov. 1.
It is greatly to the credit of director Nicholas Hytner and his team, therefore, that the evening, if it doesn’t exactly fly by, is consistently engaging, thought-provoking and downright intelligent.

cn.t: Hytner's production transforms a rarely staged Shakespeare oddity into a searing, topical parable about money and betrayal. Critics praise its caustic relevance and compelling central performance.
